## Overview

This document replicates the main empirical results of @bloom2009, which identifies uncertainty shocks using short run / recursive techniques. Data set (in all other replications as well) already come cleaned and transformed. What you see for example as x is $log(x) * 100$

## Model and Identification

Reduced-form VAR($p$):

$$y_t = c + A_1 y_{t-1} + \cdots + A_p y_{t-p} + u_t, \qquad u_t \sim (0, \Sigma)$$

Structural shocks: $u_t = B_0 \varepsilon_t$ with $\varepsilon_t \sim (0, I_K)$, so the data only pin down

$$\Sigma = B_0 B_0'.$$

Recursive (Cholesky) identification sets the upper triangle of $B_0$ to zero:

$$\Sigma = P P', \qquad B_0 = P \ \text{(lower triangular)}.$$

Structural IRFs from the Wold coefficients $\Phi_h$:

$$\Theta_h = \Phi_h B_0, \qquad h = 0, 1, \dots, H.$$

## Setup


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyMacro)
library(tictoc)

set_theme(fThemeTidyMacro())
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
dates_vec <- Bloom2009 |> pull(Date)
y         <- Bloom2009 |> select(-Date) |> as.matrix()

T <- nrow(y)
N <- ncol(y)

var_names <- colnames(y)
shockname <- "UNCERT"
shock     <- match(shockname, var_names)
```
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## VAR Estimation


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p <- 12
c <- 1

var_bloom <- fVAR(y, p, c)
sigma     <- var_bloom$sigma

# Cholesky factor (lower triangular)
S <- t(chol(sigma))

# Wold IRFs
horizon   <- 48
wold      <- fWoldIRF(var_bloom, horizon = horizon)
point_irf <- fCholeskyIRF(wold, S)
```
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Bootstrap Confidence Bands

### Standard Bootstrap


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tic()
bloom_chol <- fBootstrapChol(
    y          = y,
    var_result = var_bloom,
    nboot      = 1000,
    horizon    = horizon,
    bootscheme = "wild",
    n_threads  = 3
)
toc()
#> 2.148 sec elapsed
```
:::


### Bias-Corrected Bootstrap


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tic()
bloom_corrected <- fBootstrapCholCorrected(
    y          = y,
    var_result = var_bloom,
    nboot1     = 1000,
    nboot2     = 1000,
    horizon    = horizon,
    bootscheme = "wild",
    n_threads  = 3
)
toc()
#> 4.287 sec elapsed
```
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Impulse Response Functions

### Standard Bootstrap


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fPlotIRFChol(
    point       = point_irf,
    boot_result = bloom_chol,
    shock       = shock,
    varnames    = var_names,
    facet_ncol  = 3
) +
    labs(y = NULL)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![IRFs to uncertainty shock — standard bootstrap (68% and 90% confidence bands)](01_Bloom2009_files/figure-html/fig-irf-standard-1.png){#fig-irf-standard width=100%}
:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}

```

## Forecast Error Variance Decomposition

Share of the $h$-step forecast error variance of variable $k$ due to shock $j$:

$$\mathrm{FEVD}_{k,j}(h) = \frac{\sum_{s=0}^{h-1} (\Theta_s)_{kj}^2}{\sum_{s=0}^{h-1} \sum_{\ell=1}^{K} (\Theta_s)_{k\ell}^2}.$$


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
vardec <- fFEVDChol(point_irf, shock = shock)

fPlotVarDec(
    fevd       = vardec$fevd,
    varnames   = var_names,
    shocknames = shockname
) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tidyMacro_colors[c(2, 3)])
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Forecast error variance decomposition: share explained by uncertainty shock](01_Bloom2009_files/figure-html/fig-fevd-1.png){#fig-fevd width=100%}
:::
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Historical Decomposition

Each observation decomposes into deterministic components plus cumulated shock contributions (companion form for $p > 1$):

$$y_t = \sum_{s=0}^{t-1} \Phi^s c + \Phi^t y_0 + \sum_{s=0}^{t-1} \Theta_s \varepsilon_{t-s},
\qquad
HD_{k,t}^{(j)} = \sum_{s=0}^{t-1} (\Theta_s)_{kj}\, \varepsilon_{j,t-s}.$$


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Exclude the shock variable itself from the response variables
series <- setdiff(seq_len(N), shock)

histdec_list <- setNames(
    lapply(series, function(i) fHistDec(y, var_bloom, S, i)$histdec),
    colnames(y)[series]
)

fPlotHistDec(
    histdec_list = histdec_list,
    shock        = shock,
    shockname    = shockname,
    dates        = dates_vec,
    p            = p,
    facet_ncol   = 2
) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "7 years", date_labels = "%Y")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Historical decomposition: contribution of uncertainty shock](01_Bloom2009_files/figure-html/fig-histdec-1.png){#fig-histdec width=100%}
:::
:::
